### 2. **Session Management Submenu** (prefix + Space + S)

exec tmux display-menu -T " Session mgmt " -x R -y P \
  "Rename session"     "\$" "command-prompt -I '#S' 'rename-session -- \"%%\"'" \

### 3. **Helper Script for "Kill session & exit"**

**File**: `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/executable_kill-session-exit.sh`

Lines 1-11 contain the implementation:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Detach all clients of the current tmux session, then destroy the session.
# Gives "kill current session and return to parent shell" behavior even
# when `detach-on-destroy off` is set globally (common.conf), which would
# otherwise make `kill-session` switch to another session instead.
set -euo pipefail

session=$(tmux display-message -p '#S')
tmux detach-client -s "$session"
tmux kill-session -t "$session"
```

This script handles the "Kill session & exit" menu item, which is invoked via `run-shell` from the Session submenu.

- **Session mgmt submenu**: Generated by script, has 19 visible rows (overflows 14-row limit, see CLAUDE.md `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`)
- **Menu entry point**: `menu.sh` (line 52) calls `menu-session.sh` via `run-shell` to avoid nested-quote escaping issues
- **Submenu invocation pattern**: `exec tmux display-menu …` ensures each submenu resets quoting context independently
```

119	#
120	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)

124	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt

152	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,

154	bind M-y copy-mode \; \

192	is_vim="ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'"
193	bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-h'  'select-pane -L'
194	bind-key -n 'C-j' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-j'  'select-pane -D'
195	bind-key -n 'C-k' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-k'  'select-pane -U'
196	bind-key -n 'C-l' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-l'  'select-pane -R'
197	# NOTE: C-\ (select-pane -l) removed — tmux 3.4+ cannot parse C-\ in config files.
198	# Use directional C-h/j/k/l instead, or prefix+; for last-pane.
199	
200	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-h' select-pane -L
201	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-j' select-pane -D
202	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-k' select-pane -U
203	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-l' select-pane -R
204	{{- else -}}
205	# enableVimMode = false: vim-tmux-navigator omitted. Use prefix + h/j/k/l
206	# (kept below) or prefix + Arrow for pane navigation.
207	{{- end }}
208	
209	# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
210	bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"
211	bind - split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}"
212	
213	# Resize panes with prefix + H/J/K/L (5 cells)
214	bind -r H resize-pane -L 5
215	bind -r J resize-pane -D 5
216	bind -r K resize-pane -U 5
217	bind -r L resize-pane -R 5
218	
219	# Fine resize with Meta + h/j/k/l (1 cell, repeatable)
220	bind -r M-h resize-pane -L 1
221	bind -r M-j resize-pane -D 1
222	bind -r M-k resize-pane -U 1
223	bind -r M-l resize-pane -R 1
224	
225	# Quick ratio: set current pane to 75% width
226	bind + resize-pane -x 75%
227	
228	# =============================================================================
229	# Quick Window Switching (Ctrl+Number, requires CSI-u / extended-keys)
230	# =============================================================================
231	# Supplement to prefix + 1..9 (tmux built-in defaults, always available).
232	# These require extended-keys (CSI-u) support from the terminal emulator
233	# (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty, WezTerm). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app,
234	# plain SSH) will not send these sequences — use prefix + number instead.
235	# Note: prefix + 9 / prefix + 0 are rebound below (scode / sesh-root for
236	# current dir), so Ctrl+9 below is the only way to reach window 9 from
237	# the keyboard. Ctrl+0 mirrors prefix+0 (lightweight sesh-root) since
238	# base-index is 1 and window 0 doesn't exist.
239	
240	bind-key -n C-1 select-window -t :=1
241	bind-key -n C-2 select-window -t :=2
242	bind-key -n C-3 select-window -t :=3
243	bind-key -n C-4 select-window -t :=4
244	bind-key -n C-5 select-window -t :=5
245	bind-key -n C-6 select-window -t :=6
246	bind-key -n C-7 select-window -t :=7
247	bind-key -n C-8 select-window -t :=8
248	bind-key -n C-9 select-window -t :=9
249	bind-key -n C-0 run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
250	
251	# New window/pane inherits current path
252	bind c new-window -c "#{pane_current_path}"
253	
254	# Reload config with prefix + R
255	bind R source-file "$HOME/.tmux.conf" \; display-message "Sourced ~/.tmux.conf"
256	
257	# Session management
258	bind N command-prompt -p "New session:" "new-session -s '%%'"
259	bind X confirm-before -p "Kill session #S? (y/n)" kill-session
260	# Kill current session AND detach client (return to parent shell).
261	# Differs from `prefix + X` above, which keeps you inside tmux by
262	# switching to another session (detach-on-destroy off, common.conf).
263	# Chained via helper script because `confirm-before` takes a single
264	# tmux command; inline `\;` inside its string arg is not parsed as a
265	# command separator.
266	bind M-x confirm-before -p "Kill session #S and exit tmux? (y/n)" \
267	  "run-shell '$HOME/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh'"
268	bind x confirm-before -p "Kill pane? (y/n)" kill-pane
269	bind W confirm-before -p "Kill window #W? (y/n)" kill-window
270	
271	# Manual renumber (renumber-windows on usually handles this, but kill-pane on
272	# multi-pane windows or shell-driven exits can leave gaps).
273	bind r move-window -r \; display-message "Windows renumbered"
274	
275	# =============================================================================
276	# Move/Break Windows Across Sessions (GUI tab tear-out feel)
277	# =============================================================================
278	# prefix + M : move current window to another session (interactive prompt).
279	#              Target form: "session:" (auto-pick index) or "session:index"
280	#              (use -k via "!session:index" trick? simpler: bare prompt).
281	#              Tab-completes existing sessions.
282	# prefix + B : break current pane into a new window AND move it to a target
283	#              session in one go (acts like dragging a tab out).
284	# prefix + A : link current window into another session (window appears in
285	#              both sessions; edit either, both update). Use prefix + & to
286	#              kill, or unlink-window to detach without killing.
287	#
288	# Cross-window pane operations (no top-level prefix binding — letter slots are
289	# saturated by resize-pane H/J/K/L and sesh-last S; pane join/send live in the
290	# right-click pane menu and the popup menu's Session submenu instead):
291	#   - Mark current pane:  prefix + m  (built-in)
292	#   - Pull marked pane:   right-click pane menu → "Join marked pane here"
293	#   - Push current pane:  right-click pane menu → "Send pane to..."
294	#   - Break out to new window: right-click pane menu → "Break to new window"
295	#                              or prefix + ! (built-in, same session)
296	#                              or prefix + B (break + move to chosen session)
297	
298	bind M run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
299	  display-message "Pick destination session to MOVE window into…" \; \
300	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
301	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh move %%'"
302	bind B run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_pane '#{pane_id}'" \; \
303	  display-message "Pick destination session to BREAK pane into (as new window)…" \; \
304	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
305	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh break %%'"
306	bind A run-shell "tmux set-environment -g _src_window '#{window_id}'" \; \
307	  display-message "Pick destination session to LINK window into (window lives in both)…" \; \
308	  choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" \
309	  "run-shell '~/.config/tmux/cross-session.sh link %%'"
310	
311	# prefix + E : explode — break EVERY pane in current window into its own window
312	#              within the SAME session. Use case: switching from wide screen
313	#              (multi-pane layout) to mobile/SSH where one pane per window is
314	#              easier than zooming with prefix + z. Source window keeps the
315	#              first pane; other panes become sibling windows inserted right
316	#              after it, named after each pane's current command.
317	bind E run-shell "~/.config/tmux/break-all-panes.sh"
318	
319	# =============================================================================
320	# Theme Switching (Catppuccin <-> tmux2k)
321	# =============================================================================
322	# Note: first-time switch requires `prefix + I` to install the target plugin.
323	
324	bind M-c run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant catppuccin; \
325	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
326	  tmux display-message 'Theme: catppuccin'"
327	
328	bind M-t run-shell "tmux set -g @theme_variant tmux2k; \
329	  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf; \
330	  tmux display-message 'Theme: tmux2k'"
331	
332	# =============================================================================
333	# Sesh (tmux session manager)
334	# =============================================================================
335	
336	# prefix + g: sesh picker in a tmux popup with fzf
337	bind-key "g" run-shell "sesh connect \"$(\
338	  sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
339	    --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
340	    --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
341	    --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
342	    --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
343	    --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
344	    --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
345	    --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
346	    --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
347	    --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
348	    --preview-window 'right:55%' \
349	    --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
350	)\""
351	
352	bind -N "last-session (via sesh)" S run-shell "sesh last 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message 'No previous sesh session'"
353	
354	# prefix + 9: open repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the current
355	# pane's directory. scode walks up from cwd to find .git; if not in a repo,
356	# the error surfaces in the tmux status line.
357	# Replaces the previous `sesh connect --root $(pwd)` binding (which had a
358	# subtle bug — $(pwd) was expanded once at config parse time, not per-press).
359	# Logic is in scode-here.sh because tmux run-shell is /bin/sh (can't see

361	bind -N "scode for current dir (repo-aware coding layout)" 9 \
362	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/scode-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
363	
364	# prefix + 0: lightweight counterpart to prefix+9. Plain sesh session at
365	# the git root of the current pane's directory (no nvim/agent layout).
366	# Replaces tmux's built-in `select-window -t :=0` which always errored
367	# because base-index is 1 (no window 0 exists). Logic in sesh-root-here.sh
368	# — see that file for the two bugs in the original `sesh connect --root
369	# $(pwd)` binding (parse-time $(pwd) + misuse of --root flag).
370	bind -N "sesh-root for current dir (lightweight)" 0 \
371	  run-shell -b "~/.config/tmux/sesh-root-here.sh '#{pane_current_path}'"
372	
373	# prefix + T: sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup
374	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
375	
376	# prefix + O: sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup
377	bind-key "O" display-popup -h 90% -w 50% -E "sesh picker -i"
378	
379	# prefix + U: CLI tools picker via television (tv tools)
380	bind-key "U" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' CLI Tools (tv) ' "tv tools"
381	
382	# prefix + a: live coding-agent panes picker (tv agent-panes)
383	# Shows claude / cursor-agent / codex / opencode sessions currently running in
384	# any tmux pane. Enter switches focus to that pane. See:
385	#   docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md
386	bind-key "a" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Live agent panes (tv) ' "tv agent-panes"
387	
388	# (prefix + W is now bound earlier in this file as `kill-window`. The previous
389	# `sesh window` binding was removed because `sesh` has no `window` subcommand;
390	# pressing it printed sesh's help to a popup. See git history.)
391	
392	# =============================================================================
393	# Popup tools (display-popup -E -d '#{pane_current_path}')
394	# =============================================================================
395	# Floating scratch pane (tmux-floax) is on prefix + F (toggleable, persistent
396	# session named `float`). The bindings below are one-shot popups that close
397	# when the inner command exits — handy for "do one thing without disrupting
398	# the layout" workflows.
399	
400	# prefix + G: lazygit popup at current pane path
401	bind-key "G" display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' "lazygit"
402	
403	# prefix + ` (backtick): one-shot popup shell at current pane path.
404	# Closes when the inner shell exits (`exit` or Ctrl-D). Each invocation gets
405	# a fresh shell — no state preserved. For a persistent scratchpad with
406	# history, use floax (prefix + F) instead.
407	bind-key '`' display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' shell '
408	
409	# =============================================================================
410	# Help / cheatsheet
411	# =============================================================================
412	# tmux's built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys -N) is hard to scan and can't search
413	# user-defined bindings well. We replace it with tmux-fzf's keybinding picker
414	# (fzf popup, fuzzy-searchable). The original list-keys is still reachable on
415	# `prefix + C-?` as a fallback.
416	#
417	# `prefix + /` (built-in: prompt for a key, show what it's bound to) is left
418	# alone — it's already useful for "what does THIS key do?" lookups.
419	#
420	# `?` inside the prefix + Enter popup menu opens a glow-rendered
421	# cheatsheet (curated, grouped, prettier than list-keys).
422	
423	unbind-key '?'
424	bind-key '?' run-shell -b "~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/main.sh"
425	bind-key 'C-?' list-keys -N
426	
427	# `/` inside the Enter-popup uses this; standalone prefix + / stays built-in
428	# (key-prompt). We expose the cheatsheet through the popup menu's `?` entry.
429	bind-key M-/ display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' \
430	  "glow -p ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null \
431	    || less ~/.config/tmux/cheatsheet.md"
432	
433	# =============================================================================
434	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
435	# =============================================================================
436	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
437	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
438	#
439	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
440	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
441	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
442	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
443	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
444	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
445	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
446	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
447	#
448	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
449	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
450	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
451	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
452	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
453	#
454	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
455	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
456	# right-click on a pane / status line.
457	
458	unbind-key Space
459	unbind-key Enter
460	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
461	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
462	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
463	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
464	# in the window right-click menu).
465

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71
```

2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: edit rules and cross-file invariants. User-facing intro: [README.md](README.md).

35	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
36	
37	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
38	
39	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
40	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
41	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
42	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
43	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
44	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
45	
46	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.
47

58	
59	## Chezmoi templating conventions
60	
61	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
62	
63	| Predicate | Use |
64	|---|---|
65	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
66	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
67	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
68	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
69	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
70	
71	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
72	
73	## Hard repo invariants
74	
75	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
76	
77	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
78	
79	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
80	
81	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
82	
83	**Hard rules**:
84	
85	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
86	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
87	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
88	
89	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
90	
91	### Three-tier user-local override layer
92	
93	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
94	
95	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
96	
97	```
98	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
99	```
100
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Detach all clients of the current tmux session, then destroy the session.
# Gives "kill current session and return to parent shell" behavior even
# when `detach-on-destroy off` is set globally (common.conf), which would
# otherwise make `kill-session` switch to another session instead.
set -euo pipefail

session=$(tmux display-message -p '#S')
tmux detach-client -s "$session"
tmux kill-session -t "$session"
```

This script handles the "Kill session & exit" menu item, which is invoked via `run-shell` from the Session submenu.

- **Right-click menu**: Inline in keybindings.conf, uses `-O` flag for menu persistence
- **Session mgmt submenu**: Generated by script, has 19 visible rows (overflows 14-row limit, see CLAUDE.md `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`)
- **Menu entry point**: `menu.sh` (line 52) calls `menu-session.sh` via `run-shell` to avoid nested-quote escaping issues
- **Submenu invocation pattern**: `exec tmux display-menu …` ensures each submenu resets quoting context independently

- **Rename window (,)** - Session mgmt 選單有,window 層級。右鍵是 session 標籤可能不太對稱

**kill 動作要不要 confirm-before? (Session mgmt 選單目前都有 'y/n' 確認;現有右鍵選單沒有任何確認)**

Options:
- **Yes — 跟 Session mgmt 一致 (Recommended)** - kill session 用 confirm-before -p 'Kill session #S? (y/n)';不可逆動作有確認比較安全,且 muscle memory 跨兩個選單一致
- **No — 跟現有右鍵風格一致** - 現有右鍵選單其他動作 (Rename/New) 都沒 confirm。但 kill 是不可逆,通常還是值得確認

**Kill 動作的快捷鍵要不要對齊 Session mgmt 選單?**

Options:
- **Yes — X / E / Q (Recommended)** - 跟 prefix+Space→S 子選單一致,跨兩個選單同樣 muscle memory
- **讓我自選 (Other)** - 用其他鍵 (如 k / K) 避開現有 N/n 大寫對比


**Answer:** Kill session (X) + Kill session & exit (E), Kill all sessions (Q), Choose session... (c) — 切換 session, No — 跟現有右鍵風格一致, Yes — X / E / Q (Recommended)

```md
# Tmux status-left right-click menu: add session-level kill + switch items

## Context

`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl:82-93` defines an inline `display-menu`
bound to `MouseDown3StatusLeft` — right-clicking the session label in the
top-left status bar. The current 6-action menu (Next, Previous, Rename,
Move current window, New session, New window) covers navigation and creation
but not the **kill** and **switch-session** verbs that the user reaches for
most often.

Those same verbs already exist in the keyboard-driven Session mgmt submenu at
`dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh:5-23` (`prefix + Space → S`),
with hotkeys `X`, `E`, `Q`. Surfacing them on the right-click menu means the
session label becomes a one-click contextual entry point for the same
session lifecycle operations.

User-confirmed scope:

- Add **Kill session (X)**, **Kill session & exit (E)**, **Kill all sessions (Q)**, **Choose session... (c)**
- **No** `confirm-before` wrapper (matches the existing right-click menu's
  zero-prompt style — caller asked for parity with the right-click style, not
  the Session mgmt style)
- Hotkeys aligned with Session mgmt (`X` / `E` / `Q`) so muscle memory
  carries across both menus

## Constraints

- **Menu height ≤ terminal height** is a hard tmux constraint (`man tmux`:
  "If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed.")
  — silent failure, no error in `tmux show-messages`. See
  [pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md](../../pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
- The script-generated top menu (`menu.sh`) reads `#{client_height}` and
  tier-trims; an **inline** `display-menu` cannot. So this menu has to fit
  the smallest terminal the user actually right-clicks from.
- CLAUDE.md "Tmux popup menu" caps the top menu at ~14 visible rows. The
  right-click menu is short by default (~11) and we should stay close —
  target ≤ 14 visible rows including title.

Final layout: 10 actions + 4 separators + title bar = **15 rows**. One row
over the soft cap, but the menu is mouse-invoked from a status-bar context
(user is looking at the full status line — terminal is normal-height). The
prior version was 11 rows; we add 4 actions + 1 separator.

## Change set

**File 1**: `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` — replace lines 82-93.

\```tmux
unbind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft
bind-key -n MouseDown3StatusLeft \
  display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{session_name}" -t = -x M -y W \
    Next        n { switch-client -n } \
    Previous    p { switch-client -p } \
    "" \
    "Choose session..." c { choose-tree -Zs } \
    Rename      N { command-prompt -I "#S" { rename-session "%%" } } \
    "" \
    "Move current window to..." m { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "move-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%'" } \
    "" \
    "New session" s { new-session } \
    "New window"  w { new-window } \
    "" \
    "Kill session"        X { kill-session } \
    "Kill session & exit" E { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh" } \
    "Kill all sessions"   Q { kill-server }
\```

Notes on the diff:

- **`Choose session... c`** placed after `Next/Previous` separator and before
  `Rename` — it's the "navigate to a session by name" sibling of next/prev,
  so it belongs in the navigation group.
- **`Rename N`** keeps its existing `N` hotkey (mismatched with Session mgmt's
  `$`, but changing it would break existing muscle memory of this menu's users
  and `$` is awkward to type unshifted). Documented mismatch, leave alone.
- **`Kill session X`** reuses the existing `kill-session` command directly,
  no confirm wrapper. Note: per-tmux-config `detach-on-destroy off` means
  this **switches to another session** rather than detaching — that's why a
  separate **`Kill session & exit E`** row invokes the existing
  `~/.config/tmux/kill-session-exit.sh` helper, which detaches all clients
  *then* kills (see header comment in that script).
- **`Kill all sessions Q`** runs `kill-server` directly — destroys the whole
  tmux server, all sessions in it. User explicitly opted in with no confirm;
  this is the price of parity with the rest of the right-click menu's style.

**File 2**: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md:164` — update summary row.

\```diff
-| Session area on the left (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/rename session, move current window, new session/window |
+| Session area on the left (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/choose/rename session, move current window, new session/window, kill session/kill-and-exit/kill-all-sessions |
\```

**File 3**: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.zh-TW.md:169` — zh-TW mirror.

\```diff
-| 左側 session 區 (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/rename session、move current window、new session/window |
+| 左側 session 區 (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/choose/rename session、move current window、new session/window、kill session/kill-and-exit/kill-all-sessions |
\```

## Files NOT touched (and why)

- `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-session.sh` — the keyboard Session mgmt
  submenu already has these rows with hotkeys `X` / `E` / `Q`. No change.
- `dot_config/tmux/executable_kill-session-exit.sh` — reused as-is for the
  new "Kill session & exit" row.
- `dot_config/tmux/menu.sh` — unrelated (top-level `prefix + Space` menu).
- Cross-file maintenance table in CLAUDE.md doesn't trigger: this is not a
  Ctrl+/Alt+ keybinding, not an alias, not a shell function, not a new
  `docs/` page, not a new `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` prompt.

## Verification

End-to-end smoke (after `chezmoi apply`, inside a tmux session):

1. `tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` — verifies the template renders
   to valid tmux syntax (per CLAUDE.md "Validate app configs with the app,
   not just syntax").
2. Right-click on the session name in the status bar's top-left. Confirm:
   - 4 new rows appear at expected positions (`Choose session...`, `Kill
     session`, `Kill session & exit`, `Kill all sessions`)
   - Hotkeys `c`, `X`, `E`, `Q` activate the right rows
   - Menu fits on terminal — if it gets suppressed, `tmux show-messages` won't
     show an error (the silent-fail pitfall); reproduce by shrinking terminal
     vertically to find the cutoff height
3. Drive each new row:
   - `c` → `choose-tree` picker appears, Enter switches to that session
   - `X` on a multi-session server → current session killed, client switches
     to another session (because `detach-on-destroy off` in common.conf)
   - `E` → all clients of current session detach, session destroyed, return
     to parent shell
   - `Q` → **destructive** — only run when no work pending; verifies
     `kill-server` reachable

If `tmux source-file` rejects the new file, no live tmux session is harmed
(old config stays in memory) — just fix and re-source.

## Risk callout

`Kill session`, `Kill session & exit`, and especially `Kill all sessions`
land in the menu with **no confirmation prompt** per user request. A
mis-click on `Q` destroys every session on the server. This is the price of
parity with the existing right-click menu's no-confirm style; the Session
mgmt submenu (`prefix + Space → S`) still wraps the same actions in
`confirm-before` and remains the safer keyboard path.

158	Right-click opens a context menu depending on where you click:
159

163	| Window list (`MouseDown3Status`) | Swap left/right, move/link to session, **merge into other window as pane (h/v)**, **even layout (horizontal / vertical / tiled)**, kill window, **renumber windows**, rename, new window |
164	| Session area on the left (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/rename session, move current window, new session/window |
165
